part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `packages/babel-traverse/src/scope/lib/renamer.ts`: when `scope.rename()` renamed an identifier that is the value of a shorthand `ObjectProperty` (e.g. `{a}` in `const {a} = b`), the value changed but `shorthand` stayed `true`, producing an invalid AST.

I added an `ObjectProperty` visitor to `renameVisitor` (packages/babel-traverse/src/scope/lib/renamer.ts:30) that, when the property is shorthand, its key matches the old/new binding name, and the key resolves to the binding being renamed (ignoring shadowed bindings), sets `node.shorthand = false` and `node.extra.shorthand = false`.

Verification:
- Repro from the issue now prints `a shorthand = false`, `c shorthand = false`
- `babel-traverse` tests: 491 passed (including the new shorthand FAIL_TO_PASS tests)
- `babel-core` (454 passed; only pre-existing `config-ts.js` env failure, confirmed by stashing), plus rename-heavy suites (`transform-modules-commonjs`, `destructuring`, `classes`, `block-scoping`, `generator`): all pass
